answer: An agent economy can curb Sybil attacks using collateralized bonding inside an on-chain vault. To register, each agent locks capital whose required deposit scales with the recent churn delta of the registry. An attacker incurs an unrecoverable liquidity and capital opportunity cost per fabricated identity. Correlated actions that echo across suspicious nodes trigger collateral slashing. However, this mechanism imposes severe capital friction, excluding low-budget, legitimate agents.
